name: Aspire Cash Back Rewards Card
perks: 3% cash back on gas, groceries, and utility payments, 1% on everything else, unusual for a subprime card
Unsecured, so no security deposit required
Prequalification with a soft pull that does not hurt your score
Reports to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion)
Credit limits up to $1,000 for the strongest approved profiles
drawbacks: Annual fee is $85 to $175 the first year, then $49 plus a $5 to $15 monthly maintenance fee starting in year two (up to about $229 per year), as of mid-2026; exact fees vary by offer
Fee math: a $175 first-year fee on a $350 starting limit consumes 50% of your available credit on day one
The cash back cannot outrun the fees: you would need over $5,800 a year in 3% category spending just to cover a $175 fee, unrealistic on a limit this small
Purchase APR of 29.99% to 36% makes carrying any balance very expensive
Issued by The Bank of Missouri and serviced by Atlanticus, a fee-heavy subprime program with frequent servicing complaints
A Discover it Secured earns 2% at gas stations and restaurants with a $0 annual fee and a refundable $200 deposit; it beats Aspire on both cost and rewards for anyone who can fund the deposit
Verdict: the cash back is a distraction, not a reason to apply; only consider Aspire if you cannot fund any deposit, were declined for Mission Lane, and you land one of the lower-fee offers
